comments.note: appendChild(Node $node) is documented in the public API surface but its implementation only sets the parent pointer ($node->parent($this)) without inserting the node into the children array or rebuilding the DOM tree. Including it in an example would be misleading. It was excluded from dom_api.php and flagged here for the Reviewer to assess whether the implementation matches user expectation.

tree_traversal.php: next_sibling() / prev_sibling() in a whitespace-preserving parse may return text nodes (whitespace) before hitting the next element. The example adds a while-loop guard to skip non-element nodes. This guard pattern is worth documenting — users expecting sibling element navigation should be aware of it.

comments.note: tree_traversal.php uses a skip-whitespace while-loop guard for next_sibling/prev_sibling. This is the correct defensive pattern since whitespace text nodes appear between element siblings in a whitespace-preserving parse tree. The guard works correctly and the output confirms correct sibling elements are returned.

dom_api.php demonstrates 15 of the documented camelCase methods (AC3 requires min 12). The only omission is appendChild(), which the Developer correctly excluded given its incomplete implementation (sets parent pointer only, does not insert into children array). The debt comment from the Developer is worth escalating for Reviewer inspection.

summary: Both WP-004 files pass code review across all four dimensions.
tree_traversal.php: whitespace-skip sibling guard is the correct defensive idiom and well-demonstrated. One dead variable removed (Fix-Forward). All 9 navigation methods confirmed present.
dom_api.php: clean, systematic demonstration of 15 camelCase methods. Before/after pattern for setAttribute and removeAttribute is pedagogically strong.

appendChild() correctly excluded — its incomplete implementation (parent pointer only, no subtree insert) would mislead readers if shown as a working example. Flagged for Documentation agent to document the limitation in api-surface.md.

comments.note: tree_traversal.php: removed unused `$body = $html->find('#body', 0)` declaration. The variable was assigned upfront alongside $article, $section, and $intro, but never referenced in any section — dead code.

tree_traversal.php: the while-loop guard `while ($next !== null && $next->nodetype !== HDOM_TYPE_ELEMENT)` for next_sibling/prev_sibling is the correct defensive pattern for whitespace-preserving parses. This is worth highlighting in the docs as a named pattern for element-sibling traversal.

[documentation-forward] api-surface.md or the DOM navigation doc should clarify whether children() / childNodes() return ALL child nodes (including text/whitespace nodes) or only element children. The example adds a nodetype filter defensively — if children() already filters, the guard is redundant; if it does not, the guard is required and should be called out as a documented pattern.

[documentation-forward] api-surface.md should document that appendChild() sets only the parent pointer and does NOT insert the node into the children array. The current implementation is misleading relative to the DOM API contract — either the implementation needs finishing or the method should be marked as partial/unsupported in the public API docs. Developer debt note aligns.
